title: Grouping Living Things
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Grouping Living Things Worksheets (Vertebrates, Diets, Habitats)
standard_code: Year 4: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Recognise that living things can be grouped in a variety of ways.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on grouping living things: vertebrates and invertebrates, herbivores, carnivores and omnivores, minibeast legs, habitats and Carroll diagrams. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Group living things by what they share.
key_sub: Backbone, diet, legs or habitat: each grouping uses features you can observe.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things can be grouped in many ways, using features we can observe.

  • Animals: vertebrates or invertebrates; what they eat (herbivore, carnivore, omnivore); number of legs.
  • Plants: flowering or non-flowering. Where they live: pond, woodland, seashore.
  • Carroll diagrams sort by two yes/no questions at once.
Example

A badger eats worms and berries. Group?

Both animals and plants

Answer: omnivore

Example

A woodlouse has 14 legs. Insect?

Insects have 6 legs

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Calling a spider an insect.
  • Grouping by colour or size only.
  • Thinking every animal in water is a fish.

faq.q: How can living things be grouped?
faq.a: By features we can observe, such as whether an animal has a backbone, how many legs it has, what it eats, or whether a plant has flowers.

faq.q: What is the difference between a herbivore, a carnivore and an omnivore?
faq.a: Herbivores eat only plants, carnivores eat only other animals, and omnivores eat both.

faq.q: How does a Carroll diagram work?
faq.a: It has two yes/no questions, one across the top and one down the side, so each living thing goes in the box that matches both answers.

items.q: Is a hedgehog a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A hedgehog is a mammal.

items.q: What is an omnivore?
c: an animal that eats both plants and animals
an animal that eats only meat
an animal that eats only plants
items.e: Humans are omnivores.

items.q: Is a spider an insect?
c: No. It has eight legs, so it is an arachnid.
items.e: Count the legs.

items.q: Why do scientists group living things?
c: to make them easier to study and identify
to give them names they like
to make them all the same
items.e: Grouping shows what they share.

items.q: What is a Carroll diagram?
c: a table that sorts things by whether they have each of two features
a list of animals in size order
items.e: Yes/no rows and columns.
